overview.summary: A Heap is a specialized tree-based data structure that satisfies the heap property: the parent node is always larger (or smaller) than its children.
learningObjectives: Understand the difference between Min-Heaps and Max-Heaps.
Explain how a Heap is usually implemented under the hood using a flat Array.
Recognize 'Top K' problems as immediate Heap indicators.
overview.interviewRelevance: Heaps are the silver bullet for any question containing the phrases 'Kth largest', 'Top K frequent', or 'Merge K sorted'.

paragraphs: Imagine an emergency room. Patients don't get treated First-Come, First-Served like a normal Queue. They get treated based on the severity of their injury.
A Heap (or Priority Queue) automatically bubbles the highest priority item to the front of the line, no matter what order it arrived in.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: A Heap doesn't sort the whole array. It just guarantees that the absolute largest (or smallest) element is ALWAYS sitting at the very top.

definition.technicalDefinition: A Heap is a complete binary tree that satisfies the Heap Property. In a Max Heap, every parent node is greater than or equal to its children. In a Min Heap, every parent is less than or equal to its children.

vocabulary.definition: The process of moving an element up or down the tree to restore the Heap Property.
An abstract data type often implemented using a Heap, where elements are dequeued by priority.
A tree where every level is completely filled, except possibly the last level, which is filled left-to-right.

keyProperties: O(1) access to the Max/Min element.
Because it is a 'Complete Tree', it can be efficiently represented as a flat Array without any pointer gaps.

metaphor: A corporate ladder where any employee who performs better than their boss instantly swaps jobs with them.
mentalModel.clickSentence: By only partially sorting the data (just enough to keep the best at the top), Heaps save massive amounts of CPU time.

memoryDescription: Heaps are visually drawn as Trees, but physically stored in memory as Arrays.
Because the tree is 'Complete', we can use simple math to find children: Left Child is at (2 * index) + 1. Right Child is at (2 * index) + 2.

definitionCode.python:
import heapq
heap = []
heapq.heappush(heap, 5) # Min Heap by default
min_val = heapq.heappop(heap)

operations.name: Push (Insert)
operations.description: Add the element to the bottom (end of array), then 'Bubble Up' (swap with parent) until the heap property is restored.
operations.visualNote: A node attaches to the bottom left and floats up the tree.

operations.name: Pop (Extract Min/Max)
operations.description: Remove the root, move the very last element to the root, then 'Bubble Down' (swap with largest child).
operations.visualNote: The root disappears, the bottom-right leaf jumps to the top, then sinks down.

patternTemplate.whenToUse: Whenever a problem asks for the 'Top K', 'Kth Largest/Smallest', or asks you to repeatedly find the minimum/maximum of a changing dataset.
patternTemplate.timeComplexity: O(N log K) for finding Top K.

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: You are given a stream of 1 million incoming integers. You need to always be able to return the 5th largest integer seen so far instantly.
recognitionQuiz.explanation: Sorting 1 million items repeatedly takes O(N log N) which is too slow. A Min-Heap of size 5 tracks the top 5 largest elements in just O(N log 5) time.

examples.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
examples.problemStatement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.
steps: Push elements into the heap one by one.
If the heap size exceeds k, pop the smallest element.
At the end, the heap contains the k largest elements, and the root is the kth largest.
examples.rationale: By capping the heap size at K, we dramatically reduce memory usage and insertion time compared to a full sort.

conceptQuiz.question: If you want to find the Top K LARGEST elements, what kind of heap should you use?
conceptQuiz.explanation: Counter-intuitively, you use a MIN-Heap. You want the 'smallest of the largest' sitting at the root so you can easily pop it out when you find a bigger number.

conceptQuiz.question: How are the Left and Right children of an element at index 'i' found in a Heap array?
conceptQuiz.explanation: Because a heap is a Complete Tree, array math mathematically guarantees no empty gaps, saving memory overhead.

practice.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
practice.keyInsight: Maintain a Min-Heap of size K.

practice.title: Top K Frequent Elements
practice.keyInsight: Count frequencies with a Hash Map, then put the counts into a Min-Heap.

practice.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
practice.keyInsight: Put the head of every list into a Min-Heap to find the absolute minimum at any given moment.

practice.title: Find Median from Data Stream
practice.keyInsight: Use two heaps. A Max-Heap for the bottom half, and a Min-Heap for the top half.
